---
title: "Binary logistic regression verification record"
---

phit's `fit_logistic_matrix()` is compared with base R `glm()` and statsmodels `Logit` (Newton) on identical observations. The [executed comparison](../notebooks/logistic-verification.qmd) shows the calls and results side by side. Shared metrics are described in [Verification](../verification.qmd).

## Compared

Coefficients, covariance, standard errors, normal z tests and p-values, Wald confidence limits, fitted probabilities and response residuals, log-likelihood, deviance, null deviance, AIC, and residual df.

## Inputs and scope

Six saved R fixtures: the simulated learning sample (the multiple-predictor case), a single predictor, no intercept, intercept only, correlated full-rank columns, and imbalanced outcomes. The three-way comparison adds a listwise-deletion case with two dropped rows.

## Reference and versions

R 4.6.1, statsmodels 0.15.0 with NumPy 2.5.4 on Python 3.14.7, and phit on PHP 8.5.10, on the development Mac. Linux and PHP-FPM are not covered by this report.

- R intervals use `confint.default(fit)` (Wald), not profile-likelihood `confint(fit)`.
- R's fitting tolerance is 1e-14, so the covariance evaluated at the preceding IRLS iterate is negligible.
- Without a ones column, the null baseline is probability 0.5. The Python runner computes this convention explicitly.

## Metric and tolerance

Absolute 1e-9 plus relative 1e-7 of the R value for every numerical field. Sample accounting must match exactly. Iteration counts may differ.

## Results

All fields in all seven cases pass. The [saved report](logistic-results.json) records versions, complete outputs, maximum differences from R, warnings, and retained-row metadata.

## Known exceptions and limits

The Rust and PHP tests reject insufficient observations, invalid shapes, nonfinite values, nonbinary outcomes, one-class samples, dependent columns, and selected complete and quasi-separated designs. They also check scaled predictor units, stable arithmetic at extreme logits, iteration exhaustion, and missing-row warnings and alignment.

- No penalty or Firth correction is offered.
- The separation check is not an exhaustive linear-programming detector.
- Wald inference can be poor with sparse or nearly separated samples.

## Reproduction

From the repository root, with the PHP development tools and the [notebook environment](../notebooks/index.qmd):

```sh
cargo test --workspace --locked
cargo build -p phit --locked
php -n -d "extension=$PWD/target/debug/libphit.dylib" tests/logistic.php
.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python docs/verifications/compare_logistic.py
QUARTO_PYTHON="$PWD/.context/notebooks-venv/bin/python" \
  quarto render docs/notebooks/logistic-verification.qmd
```

Use `.so` on Linux. Regenerating the R fixtures is a separate step: `Rscript tests/generate-logistic-fixtures.R`. The Rust and PHP tests read saved fixtures and need no R or Python. [Large-sample benchmarks](../benchmarks/logistic.qmd) are reported separately.
